findings: FolderBridge mounts local/vault/WebDAV/S3/SFTP paths into Obsidian; hasAbstractFile prevents repeated virtual path notifications, not duplicate content. No content hashes or duplicate similarity decision in reviewed scanner.

Local/vault metadata batching uses concurrency8, remote1; allSettled waits for current batch, then file notifications are serial in listing order. Original function control confirms peak8 and24ordered notifications. Candidate pattern only, no Rust port or throughput claim.

First rejected stat result throws into folder-level catch; later successful entries in same batch and remaining files in that folder are abandoned. onError callback sees error, but returned result has no error/incomplete field. Synthetic control confirms zero-count result with scanLimitHit=false for first-entry failure. Callers not yet assessed.
maybeMarkHuge is called only in folder loop, not after file increments. Flat1001file control returns fileCount1001,isHuge=false. UI effects/caller behavior unverified.
Scan limit counts newly created folders and files together; existing items excluded. No cancellation token or visited-directory set in scanner. Adapter cycle/containment guarantees not yet assessed.

Reviewed upstream tests explicitly expect folder-level abort after stat failure, notification ordering and local8/remote1. Tests use synthetic dependencies/fake timers, not real Obsidian/remote storage. Test files read, Vitest not executed.

Benchmark alternates baseline/current over five repetitions of20kzero-bytefiles/100folders, checks notification equality, reports medians and admits warm OS caches/no-opnotifications. Default baselineHEAD may equal current source; no demonstrated improvement without distinct ref. Benchmark not executed.

Extension filter is case insensitive for last filename extension; markdown includes md/canvas/mdx and PDF pdf. No content or MIME validation. Manifest minimum app0.15.0 versus dev obsidian dependency^1.13.1 is not runtime compatibility proof.
